- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after a recent spike.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: it tends to forecast prices back toward historical averages, missing recent trend continuation.
- When true prices spike sharply, model forecasts lag behind and fail to capture the full magnitude of the spike.
- Model underestimates the “tail” of price increases — especially in the last 5–7 days — suggesting it underweights late-stage momentum.
- Model often overcorrects after a sharp drop, leading to a premature rebound that doesn’t match actual price behavior.
- Model shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when recent prices are high.
- Model fails to account for “price momentum carryover” — it doesn’t smoothly transition from high to low or vice versa, leading to abrupt shifts.
